recommendations.regimenLabel: Dual antiplatelet + anticoagulation + reperfusion & secondary prevention
steps: Aspirin 300 mg + a second antiplatelet (ticagrelor/clopidogrel); analgesia, oxygen only if hypoxic.
STEMI: primary PCI (or thrombolysis if PCI unavailable) — time-critical.
NSTE-ACS: anticoagulate (e.g. fondaparinux/LMWH) and risk-stratify (GRACE) for early angiography.
Start high-intensity statin, beta-blocker and ACE-inhibitor as tolerated.

drugRefs.why: Immediate antiplatelet — reduces thrombus propagation; give as soon as ACS suspected.
Second antiplatelet for dual antiplatelet therapy; more potent than clopidogrel in ACS.
Alternative P2Y12 inhibitor where ticagrelor is contraindicated (e.g. high bleeding risk, on anticoagulation).
Anticoagulation in NSTE-ACS pending angiography; favourable bleeding profile.
Alternative parenteral anticoagulant; dose-reduce in renal impairment.
High-intensity statin started early for plaque stabilisation and secondary prevention.
Reduces myocardial oxygen demand and reinfarction; start once haemodynamically stable and no acute heart failure.
ACE inhibitor for LV remodelling and secondary prevention, titrated as tolerated.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Acute Coronary Syndromes (STEMI/NSTE-ACS)
ESC 2023 Guidelines for the Management of Acute Coronary Syndromes
ACC/AHA Guideline for Coronary Artery Disease / ACS

confirm: Ischaemic chest pain ± ECG changes and troponin rise. Distinguish STEMI from NSTE-ACS by ECG.
